question: A car wash gave loyalty cards needing eight stamps, or ten stamps with two already filled. Which card was completed more often?
answer: The card with two filled: 34% of those customers earned the free wash, against 19% with the plain eight-stamp card. Nunes and Drèze called it the endowed progress effect. Both cards needed eight more washes; only one looked a fifth done. A run that seems already under way is harder to abandon.
move: Show people how far they have come, not only how far remains.
trap: Both about equally, since each card needs exactly eight more washes.
source: Nunes & Drèze, Journal of Consumer Research, 2006
reference: Nunes & Drèze, The endowed progress effect: how artificial advancement increases effort, Journal of Consumer Research, 2006
